title: Behaviour identifies a low-dimensional parameter subspace tiled by the behavioural repertoire: code, results and reproduction container
description:
Code, result files and a one-command reproduction container for a study measuring the behavioural-equivalence manifold of whole-organism nervous-system simulators — the set of parameter configurations that yield indistinguishable behaviour — across simulators spanning three phyla.

Main findings: behaviour constrains a low-dimensional stiff subspace at every parameter scale examined (5–767 parameters); in the nematode that subspace is the neural substrate of the ~4-dimensional eigenworm postural space; distinct behaviours constrain complementary rather than overlapping subspaces, so the identifiable dimension is the union over the behavioural repertoire and grows as behaviours are added; and the same organisation recurs across nematode, fly larva, rodent, an adult-fly visual circuit and the crustacean pyloric population, as well as in four external biological datasets.

The deposit contains the manuscript and Supplementary Information, every result file underlying the reported quantities, the analysis code, the input data, and a container that re-derives all reported numbers and regenerates the figures.
